items.q: Our rinse water meets USP PW. Is that enough for implants?
items.a: Not on its own. The PW monograph sets no endotoxin limit, and its microbial level is only guidance. Write both into the water specification and sample at the washer inlet.

items.q: Do we need WFI for our final rinse?
items.a: Only if your risk assessment says so, as is common for CSF contact. For most implants, PW with an endotoxin limit and point-of-use ultrafiltration costs less. We show the calculation.

items.q: How does rinse water affect our radiation dose?
items.a: Your dose is audited from device bioburden (ISO 11737-1). Rising rinse water bioburden raises device bioburden and can fail an ISO 11137-2 dose audit.

items.q: Is the water system validated or qualified?
items.a: The cleaning process is validated (ISO 13485 7.5.6, usually to ASTM F3127). The water system is qualified by IQ and OQ, with PQ from routine sampling, per GHTF SG3/N99-10.

items.q: Do you supply water for hospital reprocessing?
items.a: Reprocessing works to CSA Z314 or ANSI/AAMI ST108:2023, and the same RO and EDI platform can serve it. Our scope: [hospital, lab and industrial water scope].
